resources.string: Plug in the hub/adapter and turn on Ethernet tethering. You can still start: the servers listen on every network.
Waiting for the PS2… open OPL / NHDDL / Neutrino on the console.

Phone → USB-C hub/adapter with an Ethernet port → network cable → PS2.

Turn on Settings › Network › Hotspot & tethering › Ethernet tethering. The phone then hands out an IP on the cable.

Phone IP: %1$s
On the PS2: DHCP (OPL) or IP %2$s, mask 255.255.255.0.

No Ethernet tethering option? Some phones only have it on Android 11+ or custom ROMs (e.g. LineageOS). If the adapter is not recognized at all, try a powered hub.
Let it run in the background (battery)

Folder: a folder on the phone or the root of a USB drive (exFAT, FAT32 or NTFS) with DVD/, CD/, ART/… Works with SMB1, UDPFS and UDPBD (UDPBD sees the folder as a virtual exFAT disk).\n\nWhole USB drive (advanced): the app reads the drive directly over USB (must be exFAT or FAT32). Only UDPBD and UDPFS in block mode. Eject the drive in Settings › Storage before starting; after stopping, unplug and plug it back.

Normal: Android permissions. Since Android 11 the folder picker refuses the root of the internal storage — use the "Internal storage" button instead (it uses "all files access"). USB drives go through the picker, which is slower.

Root: reads any path (including /mnt/media_rw, the USB drive without the picker, faster). Needs Magisk/KernelSU; allow the app when asked.

Shizuku: like root, without root. Install and start the Shizuku app (wireless debugging or ADB), then pick Shizuku here and allow it.
⚠ tap the USB drive below again
Folders created. Put the .iso files in DVD (or CD).
How to set up the PS2

OPL / RiptOPL › Network Settings:
• IP Address Type: DHCP (or %2$s)
• Address: %1$s
• Port: %3$d
• Share: PS2SMB · User: guest · Password: empty
• ETH Start Mode: Auto; save and restart OPL.

Faster than SMB. Serves the folder (and the virtual disk).

NHDDL: nhddl.yaml with
 mode: udpfs
 udpfs_ip: %1$s
Neutrino: config/bsd-udpfs.toml → args = ["ip=%1$s"]
RiptOPL: use the same PS2 IP as in the network settings.

Block device: the PS2 sees an exFAT disk (the folder as a virtual disk, or the whole USB drive).

Neutrino: config/bsd-udpbd.toml → args = ["ip=%1$s"]
RiptOPL / XEB+: UDPBD device, with PS2 IP %1$s.
Tap the USB drive again to allow access
No permission to use the USB drive
That folder isn\'t on the phone or USB drive storage
Android didn\'t grant permanent access to this folder
Still checking the folder, try again in a moment
Shizuku isn\'t running. Open the Shizuku app and start it.
⚠ NTFS drive: in block mode the PS2 only reads exFAT/FAT32. Use Folder mode (works with NTFS) or format it as exFAT.
⚠ No exFAT/FAT32 found on this disk; the PS2 may not see the games in block mode.
USB drive not found (was it unplugged?)
↳ Another app is already using this port (another SMB/PS2 server?). Close it or restart the phone.
↳ The hub\'s network adapter dropped for a moment. If it keeps happening: use a hub with its own power supply, check the USB-C plug, or try another hub/cable.
↳ The PS2 stopped answering mid-transfer: the cable/hub flickered, or the game froze on the console (try another mode or loader settings).
↳ If the game froze now, the connection dropped: check the cable, the hub power and that the phone screen-off/battery saver didn\'t cut the network.
↳ Failed to read the game file: USB drive loose or without power, folder access revoked, or a damaged file.
↳ That client isn\'t OPL: only SMB1 is supported (OPL and RiptOPL use SMB1).
↳ The root/Shizuku access stopped (Shizuku restarted, or root was revoked). Stop and start again.
⚠ No network on the cable. Check: hub plugged in and powered, cable in the PS2, Ethernet tethering on.
⚠ The PS2 (%1$s) is not on the cable network (%2$s). Its IP should look like %3$s; replies may go out through Wi-Fi.
⚠ Android may pause the server with the screen off. Tap \"Let it run in the background\".
